project.name: FitFlow Trainer Platform
project.description: Multi-tenant trainer-client platform with AI RAG workout generation, billing flows, chat, role-based access, and trainer/client dashboards.
project.roadmap:
# FitFlow Platform Roadmap

## Phase 1 - Foundation (Weeks 1-3)
- Identity and authorization model finalized
- Trainer-client relationship scoping enforced at API level
- Core data model and audit logging baselines

## Phase 2 - Core Product (Weeks 4-7)
- Workout planning domain and schedule lifecycle
- Trainer-client chat MVP with delivery states
- Trainer and client dashboard initial slices

## Phase 3 - AI & Intelligence (Weeks 8-10)
- RAG retrieval corpus and indexing strategy
- Context-safe prompt orchestration and explainable output
- Workout generation with contraindication policy checks

## Phase 4 - Monetization & Ops (Weeks 11-13)
- Billing ledger + fee split implementation
- Webhook handling and settlement reconciliation
- Notification orchestration and operational observability

## Exit Criteria
- Epic tickets decomposed into implementable child tasks
- Service-level API specs maintained and aggregated into project apiSpec
- Security and authorization tests passing for role + relationship boundaries

- WorkoutPlan (programId, generatedBy, rationale)

- MessageThread (trainerId, clientId)

project.readmeMd:
# FitFlow Trainer Platform

FitFlow is a multi-tenant coordination platform for trainers and clients.

## Core capabilities
- Secure trainer/client relationship authorization
- AI-assisted workout generation using RAG over trainer and client context
- Trainer-client chat with status and attachment governance
- Financial flows: trainee pays trainer; trainer pays platform fee
- Trainer and client dashboards with role-specific access boundaries

## Delivery model
- Large initiatives tracked as EPIC tickets
- Child sub-tickets represent small, testable implementation units
- Each service owns its API spec; project apiSpec is an aggregate artifact

## Non-functional priorities
- Strict authorization consistency (token == user privileges)
- Auditable financial and privileged action trails
- Explainable AI outputs with safety constraints
- Reliable event handling and idempotent webhooks

tickets.title: [EPIC] Trainer & Client Dashboards
tickets.description:
Deliver actionable dashboards for trainers and trainees with progress, adherence, billing, and communication views.

Acceptance:
- Trainer KPIs and client rollups
- Client plan progression and next actions
- Role-specific data boundaries

tickets.title: [EPIC] Trainer-Client Chat & Collaboration
tickets.description:
Implement secure trainer-client messaging with attachment support and event tracking.

Acceptance:
- Conversation authorization by relationship
- Message delivery/read status
- Moderation and audit trails

tickets.title: [EPIC] Billing, Fees & Settlement
tickets.description:
Enable trainee-to-trainer billing and trainer-to-platform fee model with ledger-grade records and reconciliation.

Acceptance:
- Subscription/invoice lifecycle
- Fee split and payout scheduling
- Webhook-driven payment state updates

tickets.title: [EPIC] AI RAG Workout Generation
tickets.description:
Build AI pipeline that generates safe workouts using trainer playbooks, client profile/history, goals, injuries, and equipment context.

Acceptance:
- Retrieval index for knowledge artifacts
- Prompt + safety policy orchestration
- Explainable workout output with rationale

tickets.title: [EPIC] Identity, Access & Tenant Security
tickets.description:
Implement robust authn/authz: trainer/client/admin roles, trainer-client association scopes, token/permission model, and auditing.

Acceptance:
- JWT + PAT enforcement aligned with user permissions
- Relationship-based authorization guard coverage
- Admin role management and pending approval flow

protocol.goal: Token permissions must mirror user permissions. Never perform actions the user could not perform in the UI.

workDecomposition.epicRule: Large features must be created as Epic tickets first.
workDecomposition.subTicketRule: Epic implementation work must be decomposed into child sub-tickets with specific deliverables.
workDecomposition.effortBias: Prefer XS/S/M child tickets. Avoid L/XL unless unavoidable.

whenUnspecified: Only consider tickets in accessible projects and exclude DONE/CANCELLED.
First prefer IN_PROGRESS tickets already assigned to the acting user.
If multiple candidates remain: priority (CRITICAL>HIGH>MEDIUM>LOW), then smallest effort, then oldest updated.
If blocked, record blocker context and pick the next ranked candidate.
If no suitable ticket exists, create an Epic and immediately create child sub-tickets before starting work.
Before execution, state selected ticket ID and one-line reason.

apiSpecPolicy.sourceOfTruth: Per-service API specs are the source of truth.
apiSpecPolicy.aggregation: Project-level apiSpec must be generated from service-level specs.
updateOrder: Then update project apiSpec as composed output.

safety: Stop and report when access is forbidden.
Do not perform cross-project mutations without access.
